Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication:  Knee pain.. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Intact. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

The meniscal body also demonstrates complex tearing involving the free edge and the undersurface.

Intrasubstance degeneration in the anterior horn. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  High-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss involving the central to posterior aspects of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild subchondral edema. Small central and marginal osteophytes. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Intact.

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse mild thinning of the patellar cartilage. There is high-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the trochlea, maximal centrally and laterally, with multifocal subchondral bone marrow edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

2. Moderate lateral and patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion and small popliteal cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain. Positive medial meniscus testing. 
Comparison: [REDACTED]. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. No popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: High-grade radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction. Large degree of peripheral meniscal extrusion, with the meniscus projecting 5 mm beyond the tibial margin. There is also a horizontal tear of the meniscal body and oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  There is full-thickness cartilage loss involving the weightbearing portions of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild to moderate subchondral bone marrow edema. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Bowing of the ligament secondary to meniscal extrusion. 

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse thinning of the patellar cartilage, with high-grade and small full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial patellar facet. There is also multifocal cartilage fissuring of the lateral patellar facet. Partial-thickness cartilage loss is noted in the central and medial aspect of the trochlea. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Complex tear of the medial meniscus, including radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction, with peripheral extrusion.

2. Moderate medial greater than patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion. 


Signed By: [NAME] 
 Signed On: [DATE]

In the medial compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is diffuse low grade and high grade chondrosis along weight-baring, non weight-baring medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes 
 The lateral compartment, there is radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. There is diffuse low grade chondrosis along weight-baring lateral femoral condyle. Focal high grade chondrosis with subchondral edema at lateral tibial plateau (about 1.8* 2 cm). Osteophytes are present.  
 The patellofemoral joint, there is diffuse low grade chondrosis (less than 50% thickness cartilage loss) along medial, lateral patellar facets, medial and lateral trochleas. There is no subchondral edema. Osteophytes are present. The medial patellofemoral ligament is intact.  
 There is chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. There is anterior tibial translation. 
 There is chronic partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament. Chronic partial tears of the medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes are suspected. The extensor mechanism is normal.  
 Large amount of effusion with synovitis is present in right knee including popliteus recess. There are multiple osteocartilaginous loose bodies (about 1-2.5 cm) in right knee including suprapatellar bursa and popliteal recess. The surrounding musculature is normal.   -- Moderate tri-compartmental osteoarthritis of the right knee by evidence of chondrosis, subchondral edema, cysts and osteophytes. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
 -- Radial tear at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.  
 -- Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament, at mid substance.  
 -- Chronic partial tear of the posteromedial oblique ligament.  
 -- Chronic partial tears of the medial and lateral collateral ligament complexes. 
 -- Large amount of effusion with synovitis and multiple loose bodies (about 1-2.5 cm) in right knee including suprapatellar bursa and popliteal recess: probable for secondary synovial osteochondromatosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain for one week.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Healed non-ossifying fibroma at the distal femoral metaphysis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. Moderate extrusion of the body without discrete tear by MRI criteria.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade fissuring at the notch third of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss with subchondral edema and cystic change at the medial patellar facet and median ridge. Full thickness fissuring of the lateral facet. Partial thickness cartilage loss with full-thickness fissuring at the central and lateral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar tilt. No lateral translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
High-grade patellofemoral compartment chondrosis. Low-grade medial and lateral compartments chondrosis.

COMPARISON:Plain films [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Twisting injury 4 weeks prior. Suspected transient lateral patellar dislocation.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact. Popliteus tendon insertion is intact.

No femoral trochlear dysplasia. No patellofemoral subluxation. The TT-TG distance measures 20 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact. Once again seen are well-corticated osseous fragments at the tibial tuberosity in keeping with chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease. Minimal marrow edema and tiny cysts are noted in the fragments. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Full-thickness cartilage denuding patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Preserved medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, predisposing to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
2. High-grade patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving moderate patellofemoral osteoarthritis of the left knee.
3. Chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease, also shown previously.
4. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular:Medial menisküs diz ekleminde 4,5mm mediale ekstrüdedir. Menisküste maserasyon , volüm kaybı ve kompleks yırtıklar izlendi. Lateral menisküs anterior -posterior hornu ve gövde kesiminde grade II dejenerasyon izlendi.Anterior çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyona sekonder kalınlaşma ve sinyal artışı izlendi.Arka çapraz bağ, lateral  kollateral ligaman normaldir.Medial kollateral ligamende periligamentöz ödem izlendi ( grade I sprain ).Patella medial fasette kartilaj bütünlüğünde kayıp izlendi. Lateral fasette kartilajda incelme, subkondral kemik iliği ödemi izlendi.Suprapatellar bursa ve diz eklem mesafesinde sıvı artışı izlendi.Femur medial kondil postero-süperior kesim komşuluğunda ekstraartiküler yerleşimli 2,5x1,5 cm boyutlu ganglion kisti izlendi.Diz eklemi kapsülü posteriorunda yırtık ve yırtık ile ilişkili 2x1,5cm boyutlu ganglion kisti izlendi.Tibia interkondiler eminenc anteriorunda anterior çapraz bağ yapışma yeri düzeyinde 1cm çaplı subkortikal kist izlendi.Peripatellar cilt altı yağ dokuda ödem izlendi.Tibia femoral eklem medialde eklem aralığında daralma , ekleme komşu kemik yüzlerde subkondral skleroz ödem ve dejeneratif kistler izlendi. Bu düzeyde femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda destrüksiyon izlendi. Bulgular dejeneratif artrit lehine yorumlandır.Femur lateral kondilde subkondral alanda 6x4mm boyutlu osteokondral defekt izlendi. Diz eklemini oluşturan her üç kompartmanda santral -marjinal osteofit formasyonu izlendi. Sonuç: Gonartroz, medial menisküste mediale ekstrüzyon, maserasyon , volüm kaybı ve kompleks yırtıklar , lateral menisküste grade II meniskopati, anterior çapraz bağda mukoid dejenerasyon, medial kollateral ligamende grade I sprain , suprapatellar bursit, diz ekleminde sinovit,  ekstraartiküler ganglion kisti, tibia interkondiler eminencde subkortikal kist, prepatellar cilt altı ödem, diz eklem kapsülü posteriorunda yırtık ve yırtık ile ilişkili ganglion kisti, patella medial fasette grade III lateral fasette grade II kondromalazi.
